causal_variable.definition: Salience and weight of an explicit objective to minimize or reduce spending across tasks.

inferred_variable.variable: Incentive framing of the agent’s goal orientation toward cost containment versus service continuity
inferred_variable.definition: The extent to which the subject agent is instructed and evaluated to prioritize budget minimization and price sensitivity, as opposed to prioritizing uninterrupted operations, when making procurement decisions.
inferred_variable.evidence: Across the simulations, the subject-agent role description systematically shifts from operations-first with minimal savings pressure (e.g., not expected to seek savings beyond prudence) to balanced cost/service trade-off, and then to strong cost-control language emphasizing challenging requests, deferring buys, and reducing outlays. The background environment, actors, budget, inventory dynamics, and requisition stream remain essentially the same, so the main changing factor is the motivational/evaluative framing applied to the agent. The observed decisions track this shift: operations-priority versions approve fuller and faster replenishment, while cost-focused versions negotiate lower prices, use remanufactured batteries, phase optional buys, and defer safety stock.

Separately, allowing a critical item to run out because you did not arrange timely replenishment triggers a major service disruption event recorded at the time the stockout occurs.
